**Static Length-Based Routing** sends prompts to a small or large model based on a fixed token-length threshold. *Cost*: Low (no extra inference), but inefficient—short prompts may overuse the large model, while long ones strain the small model. *Latency*: Minimal overhead, but the small model may struggle with complex long prompts, increasing processing time. *Failure Modes*: Poor accuracy if length doesn’t correlate with complexity; small model may fail on "short but hard" prompts.

**Classifier-Based Routing** uses a lightweight model to predict which model to use. *Cost*: Higher (extra inference step), but more efficient long-term by optimizing model selection. *Latency*: Adds classifier latency (~10-50ms), but reduces overall latency by avoiding mismatches. *Failure Modes*: Classifier errors may route prompts suboptimally; requires training data and maintenance.

**Trade-off**: Static is simpler and cheaper for predictable workloads; classifier is better
